HCPortal 496.summary: Malsburg reports that he does not know where the garrisons' upkeep is to come from now that the contributions from the open country have ended, and urges that a safe-conduct for the envoys to the peace talks at  be solicited from the King of Hungary.
HCPortal 496.en:
⟨… made,⟩ that I still do not know where our garrisons' upkeep is to be taken from hereafter, which consists in grain ⟨and⟩ [201]; ⟨since⟩ the contributions from the open country, both here and in [239], are at an end. ⟨And⟩ one will now every month [give?] to <+> […]tman [193] ⟨and⟩ <f> [273] in [210] twelve <4#> quarters, Kassel quarters; because the non-commissioned officers receive double rations ⟨and⟩ [144] […] have.

It is still time for one to present oneself to the King of Hungary about the peace negotiations ⟨and⟩ to solicit a safe-conduct for <H#> envoys to {Cologne}. [176] will not begin to negotiate without [140]. On this present campaign a great deal [?depends]; therefore days of prayer are [?most needful].

- "Commis" = commissary bread, the soldier's ration. "Viertel" = the Kassel grain measure.
- "[give?]" is the translator's guess at the sense of the holed clause;

HCPortal 497.summary: From Wesel: he does not know whether to go to  or to the army; the recruits and Dalwig's Verehrungsgelder, Eberstein's regiment, and the impossibility of travelling through Friesland with wagons and horses; word that it was decided at Regensburg to give the envoys to  no safe-conduct, and of talks apart at  or Lübeck.
HCPortal 497.en:
⟨… will maintain as long as possible,⟩ I do not now know how I [?should] set about the journey, ⟨and⟩ whether <H#>
[should] still be at [148] or with the army [?…], [whether] a journey should still go ahead, ⟨and⟩ <XX> [could or
would] send my [?dispatch] [259] or [258]; much time would be [?…] ⟨that what I …⟩

⟨… and the Lord Statthalter has not yet come back,⟩ that I can take with me the recruits ⟨and⟩ the gratuities for
Dalwig's ⟨and⟩ Eberstein's {regiment}, as well as [?the] [?life guard], ⟨I will, by the messengers sent by the Lord
…,⟩ and [?…] or by the bearer [wait for] {the States'} order for my further conduct, whether I <6> should seek means
alone at [129] for the costs, or bring the train left here with me; for to go through Friesland with wagons ⟨and⟩
horses is impossible.

HCPortal 497, letter block.summary: A separate ten-line block in a letter cipher with repeating shifts 4, 5, 3, 6, 2, deciphered by Larry Beck with ChatGPT; the selected reading discusses command, the Swedish generals, the reciprocal joining of forces and the authority requested. A working edition: the code labels 43, 45 and LL are unidentified.
HCPortal 497, letter block.en:
The [43] is now on the point of leaving. If [45] wish to be rid of him and can do without him, it is now time for
[LL] to write: since they see that he †would† not come to agreement with the Swedish generals over the command, but
the state of [45] required that they join their †troops† [?troops] to the Swedes and the Swedes in turn to them, and
also [LL]'s actions no longer pleased him, and moreover they could not give him such absolute authority as he
demanded, they left it to what [?pleased] him to do; nor would they keep him back against his convenience, but would
have him satisfied according to [?their] †present† [?present] state and ability.

HCPortal 502.summary: The provisioning of Hermannstein (Ehrenbreitstein); Obrist Hoffman's troops; marches by Marburg, Corbach and Brilon on the road from ; Jan de Werth at Cologne.

HCPortal 503.summary: No audience yet; notice of the end of the Stillstand; companies and dragoons, with recruiting patents already issued; the ambassador of ; money and horses.

HCPortal 504.summary: Some of the  are so frozen that several have become cripples; the obligation over the loss before Hermannstein; the new recruiters.

HCPortal 505.summary: The dispute over whether Hermannstein was effectively provisioned; ransom and gifts for the commanders; the finding that 'we have dealt with a Frenchman'; peace talks in Picardy with nobody sent to ; a separate peace with the imperial commissioners; the garrisons ruined.

HCPortal 506.summary: has resolved to content the Reuter; ransom for prisoners; letters of exchange.
HCPortal 506.en:
⟨… is to be expected,⟩ [120] has now resolved to satisfy the carters; but as for the carriage money, the ransom for the
prisoners ⟨and⟩ other costs, he will not yet agree to that, but refers us to the 9 thousand Reichsthaler received,
which [143] [?has had] paid out. The <H#> letter to <V> of <L> January has now come to the [122] for the fourth time,
⟨and⟩ I press him daily to go after his brother ⟨and⟩ into the [123] ⟨and⟩ put his private affairs in order, so that,
when an opportunity offers to come through ⟨and⟩ to {Cologne}, he may not only leave quickly ⟨and what also⟩ could
stay for a while in Hesse. He is indeed willing to come to {the States}, but to remain at [148] - he has, it seems to
me, little desire for that, ⟨and⟩ <XX> will hardly be able to rely on it.

HCPortal 507.summary: The journey by the Watten; twelve-pound cannon and constables; Jan de Werth between Ruhr and ; the States' alliance and a muster place in Cleves; the conjunction at Cloppenburg, Quakenbrück, Minden, Vechta, Wildeshausen and Diepholz.
HCPortal 507.en: ⟨I arrived back safely yesterday evening … and found Your Princely Grace's gracious letter … there,⟩ I would indeed like to set out from here with <H#> train as soon as possible ⟨and⟩ by land, since Dunkirkers were lying on the Watten a few days ago, and arrive by [235] at the appointed place with God's help. But since I am to bring [193] [212] guns ⟨and⟩ [197] <V>, and the enemy (who, between [149] ⟨and⟩ the Ruhr, has about 6 {companies} [193] <e> <n> {companies} [200] ⟨and⟩ 1 {company} of dragoons [?lying], and besides <K> {regiment} [212] from Lorraine, about <4#> [?horse] strong, coming to join) now gathers ⟨and⟩ wants to take the field, it is not advisable to go overland; by water, though, it is slow ⟨and⟩ cannot be put in hand so quickly, for it takes a great deal of time before ships that go to sea ⟨and⟩ are not to be had here are ordered;

HCPortal 508.summary: The duplicate of the 28 March letter, re-copied with different line breaks; used only as a check copy and not deciphered or counted separately, so its text is that of HCPortal 507 (blocks 'work/f028.txt' and 'work/f029.txt').

HCPortal 509.summary: A French letter signed '232' of 3 Apr 1637, citing a letter of the ambassador extraordinary in London, and German news extracts from London of 16/26 Mar in a second hand, in the same key; paired large capitals are name signs.

system: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
